jobs.title: Summer Games Software Developer Intern - Colorado Springs, Colorado at Booz Allen Hamilton Inc
jobs.description: Employer: Booz Allen Hamilton Inc Expires: 10/17/2026 University, 2027 Summer Games Software Developer InternThe Opportunity: The Summer Games is an innovative internship program that attracts some of the nation’s best and brightest students. The goal is to develop a breakthrough idea or solution for one of our customer's most pressing, complex, and multidimensional problems while developing valuable technical skills. This competitive and collaborative program attracts thousands of applicants each year. Simulating a real-world startup accelerator environment, the interns are divided into teams, each working on a different challenge project. Throughout the Games, interns receive mentorship from senior leaders, solve problems using Booz Allen’s products and unique engagement models, and leverage the power of collaboration in a team environment. The summer culminates with a final Challenge Cup competition and presentation to senior leadership. A past winner took the challenge of helping blind individuals navigate by using new technology and developing a business and market penetration plan. Teams have also helped to develop an app that gives military commanders an easy way to track real-time and open-source information about developing situations, including sudden attacks, fighting human trafficking, and even tracking the spread of a disease worldwide. Join us. The world can't wait. You Have: Experience with programming languages, including Java, JavaScript, C, C++, Assembly, Python, Perl, R, or Bash Experience with machine learning, data mining, statistics, or graph algorithms in academic or internship environments Experience with conducting research and writing software Ability to produce technical documentation and create design artifacts Ability to work independently and in teams Ability to obtain a Secret clearance Scheduled to obtain a Bachelor’s degree in a Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics field by Winter 2027 or 2028, or Spring 2028 or 2029 Nice If You Have: Ability to produce technical documentation and create design artifacts Possession of excellent critical thinking and analytical skills Possession of excellent verbal and written communication skills Clearance: Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. CompensationAt Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page. Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $52,900.00 to $108,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date. Identity StatementAs part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. Candidate AI Usage PolicyAI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided. Work ModelOur people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration, whether it occurs in person or virtually. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen facility frequently, in alignment with leadership expectations and the needs of the role. You may also be required to work from or visit a customer facility.Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed at a Booz Allen office or customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role. jobs.title: CLIA Lab Operations Intern at Complete Omics Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Complete Omics Inc. Expires: 10/17/2026 Job Description:Compensation: Negotiable internship compensation based on qualifications, experience, and time commitment.Complete Omics Inc. is a venture-backed, commercial-stage biotechnology company located in the Baltimore, Maryland area. We develop and commercialize advanced omics-based platforms and solutions for precision medicine, health monitoring, and disease diagnostics.Complete Omics has two immediate openings for CLIA Laboratory Operations & Bioinformatics Interns. These positions offer students and recent graduates a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a highly translational biotechnology and clinical laboratory environment.Complete Omics provides a particularly distinctive training environment. While many academic and biotechnology laboratories conduct proteomics or multi-omics research, relatively few combine advanced mass spectrometry-based proteomics and multi-omics technologies with CLIA-regulated clinical laboratory operations.At Complete Omics, interns will have the opportunity to work at the intersection of clinical laboratory medicine, mass spectrometry-based proteomics and metabolomics, bioinformatics, laboratory informatics, and patient data systems. This provides rare exposure to how advanced omics technologies are translated from research and assay development into regulated clinical workflows supporting patient testing and precision medicine.Interns may gain hands-on experience across the complete translational pathway:Patient sample → CLIA laboratory workflow → proteomics/multi-omics analysis → bioinformatics → quality control → clinical data interpretation → patient-level reportingThis combination of CLIA laboratory operations and advanced proteomics/multi-omics technologies makes the internship particularly valuable for students interested in clinical diagnostics, biotechnology, precision medicine, computational biology, bioinformatics, or careers at the interface of laboratory science and healthcare technology.What Interns Can LearnThis internship provides exposure to the complete translational process, from patient sample handling and clinical laboratory testing through mass spectrometry, bioinformatics, quality control, data interpretation, and patient-level reporting.Interns may gain experience in:CLIA laboratory operationsClinical assay development and validationPrecision medicine and molecular diagnosticsClinical proteomics and metabolomicsMass spectrometry-based multi-omicsLaboratory automation and workflow optimizationBioinformatics pipeline developmentPatient data management and analysisLaboratory Information Management System (LIMS) developmentClinical data quality controlScientific software and informatics developmentTranslational research and biotechnology commercializationHigh-performing interns may have opportunities to take on increasingly independent projects and contribute to scientific publications, assay and technology development, bioinformatics systems, and future clinical products.Position DetailsJob Title: CLIA Laboratory Operations & Bioinformatics InternPosition Type: InternshipLocation: OnsiteComplete Omics Inc.1448 South Rolling RoadHalethorpe, Maryland 21227United StatesSchedule: Full-time or part-time internship opportunities may be available depending on the candidate's academic schedule, availability, and project needs.Work Location: In personNumber of Positions: 2Work AuthorizationU.S. work authorization requiredCandidates with CPT or OPT authorization are welcome to applyVisa sponsorship may be considered where applicableApplicationPlease submit a resume/CV and cover letter describing your background, interests, and relevant laboratory, computational, bioinformatics, or software development experience.Candidates are encouraged to indicate whether they are particularly interested in CLIA laboratory operations, proteomics/multi-omics, bioinformatics and patient data systems, or a combination of these areas.

jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineering Intern at Gecko Robotics, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Gecko Robotics, Inc. Expires: 10/17/2026 Role at a GlanceGecko Robotics is seeking a Full Stack Software Engineering Intern to join our Engineering team in New York for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.Gecko’s Engineering teams build customer-facing applications that turn robot, sensor, and document data into decisions about the health of critical infrastructure. You will work across the stack on a defined project: building frontend workflows, backend services, and data pipelines that make complex asset data usable by the people who maintain it. You will ship real features into a product that customers already rely on, with clear direction from a mentor and the room to own your piece of it.Due to government program requirements, candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.What you will doOwn a scoped full-stack project from design through deployment under the guidance of experienced engineers.Build user-facing features in React and TypeScript that support real operational workflows.Develop backend APIs and services in Python that ingest, transform, and serve structured and unstructured data.Design data models and schemas, and write the logic that parses, associates, and validates data from multiple sources.Use version control, code review, testing, and structured debugging to produce maintainable code.Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and Forward Deployment Engineers to understand how customers use the product, with the option to travel to a customer site during the summer.Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship.Technologies We UseReact, TypeScript, Python, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Git, Linux, and cloud infrastructure (GCP). Depending on the project, you may also work with LLM APIs and data-processing pipelines, 3D visualization, or containerized deployments. The specific tools will depend on the assigned project.About YouYou are a builder who likes seeing your work used. You are comfortable moving between frontend and backend, you break large problems into shippable pieces, and you communicate clearly about what you built, what you learned, and what you would do next.Required SkillsCurrently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.Ability to work onsite in New York, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.Foundational programming experience in Python and JavaScript or TypeScript, including object-oriented or functional programming concepts.Experience building a web application end to end (frontend and backend) through coursework, projects, research, hackathons, or a prior internship.Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.Understanding of relational databases and REST APIs.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback.Preferred SkillsExperience with React and TypeScript in a real project.Experience designing data schemas or working with messy, real-world datasets.Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP, and to containers such as Docker.Exposure to integrating LLM or other AI APIs into an application.Interest in 3D, visualization, or spatial data.Interest in industrial, defense, or infrastructure applications where reliability matters.

Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit. Experienced Human Resources Leadership Development Program InternshipJohnson & Johnson’s Experienced HR Leadership Development Program (E-HRLDP) is consistently ranked as one of the top Leadership Development Program in Human Resources by MBA-Exchange.com (as voted by students from over 100 MBA schools globally).This best-in-class HRLDP is designed to develop experienced professionals in their journey to become the global HR leaders of tomorrow, through:Unmatched depth of broad-based experience across the J&J operating modelA prescriptive two-year Development Journey designed to support your on-going development.Relationships spanning our global businesses, HR community and executive leadership.E-HRLDP Internship Program:The E-HRLDP Internship is a 10-12 week program enabling highly motivated graduate students to demonstrate their potential to be one of Johnson & Johnson’s HR Leaders of the future. What we prefer you bring:Familiarity with GIS applications, Civil 3D, HEC-RAS, or HEC-HMS.Compensation:The salary range for this role is $21.00 - $28.00 per hour. jobs.title: Postdoctoral Researcher at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 10/17/2026 A post-doctoral research opportunity is available through the Department of Operational Sciences at the Air Force Institute of Technology.What will I be doing?As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will join a community of scientists and researchers studying adversarial interactions, multi-agent systems, and decision-making under uncertainty relevant to security and defense settings. Research activities will focus on methodological innovation, theoretical development, and applied mathematical/statistical modeling.Why should I apply?Under the guidance of a mentor, you will gain hands-on experience to complement your education and support your academic and professional goals. Along the way, you may engage in activities and research in several areas. These include, but are not limited to:Adversarial location and network interdiction modelsAdversarial machine learning attacks and defense (e.g., against Bayesian inference)Algorithmic development for bilevel (or multilevel) optimizationMethodological developments in Bayesian statistics and/or decision analysisApplication of adversarial risk analysis within security settingsWhere will I be located? Dayton, OhioWhat is the anticipated start date?Exact start dates will be determined at the time of selection and in coordination with the selected candidate. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis and fellowships will be filled as qualified candidates are identified.What is the appointment length? This appointment is a twelve-month research appointment, with the possibility to be renewed for additional research periods. Appointments may be extended depending on funding availability, project assignment, program rules, and availability of the participant.What are the provisions? You will receive a stipend to be determined by AFIT. Stipends are typically based on a participant’s academic standing, discipline, experience, and research facility location. Other provisions may include the following:Health Insurance Supplement (Participants are eligible to purchase health insurance through ORISE)Relocation AllowanceTraining and Travel AllowanceAbout AFITThe Air Force Institute of Technology, or AFIT, located at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the Air Force’s graduate school of engineering and management as well as its institution for technical professional continuing education. A component of Air University and Air Education and Training Command, AFIT is committed to providing defense-focused graduate and professional continuing education and research to sustain the technological supremacy of America’s air, space and cyber forces.About ORISEThis program, administered by Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and DoD. Participants do not enter an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DoD or any other office or agency. Instead, you will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE. For more information, visit the ORISE Research Participation Program at the U.S. Department of Defense.Qualifications The qualified candidate should hold or be currently pursuing a doctoral degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Statistics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a closely related field. A postgraduate is required to have earned their degree within 5 years of the appointment start date.A PhD is not required at the time of selection. Ideally, a participant will complete their PhD prior to the opportunity's start date; however, an "all but dissertation" status may be acceptable as well, provided the requisite research qualifications.Preferred Skills:Background in quantitative research, evidenced by peer-reviewed publications, academic presentations, or preprint manuscriptsKnowledge of Bayesian statistics, mathematical optimization, game-theoretic analysis, network problems, decision analysis, or behavioral economicsProficiency in a scientific computing or statistical programming languages (e.g., Python, R, Julia, C++, or MATLAB)Familiarity with mathematical programming solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) or probabilistic/Bayesian computing frameworks (e.g., Stan, PyMC)Ability to formulate high-impact, novel and well-defined research questions from unstructured requirementsApplication RequirementsA complete application consists of:Zintellect ProfileEducational and Employment HistoryEssay Questions (goals, experiences, and skills relevant to the opportunity)Resume (PDF)Transcripts/Academic Records - Please upload a copy of a transcript for your current or most recent degree program that meets the disciplinary qualifications of the opportunity. Click here for detailed information about acceptable transcripts.One Recommendation. We encourage you to contact your recommender(s) as soon as you start your application to ensure they are able to complete the recommendation form and to let them know to expect a message from Zintellect. Recommenders will be asked to rate your scientific capabilities, personal characteristics, and describe how they know you. You can always log back in to your Zintellect account and check the status of your application.If you have questions, send an email to AIRFORCE@orise.orau.gov. Please list the reference code of this opportunity [AFIT-2026-0022] in the subject line of the email. Please understand that ORISE does not review applications or select applicants; selections are made by the sponsoring agency identified on this opportunity. All application materials should be submitted via the “Apply” button at the bottom of this opportunity listing. Please do not send application materials to the email address above.Connect with ORISE...on the GO! Download the new ORISE GO mobile app in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to help you stay engaged, connected, and informed during your ORISE experience and beyond!Stipend $6,500.00 – $8,250.00 MonthlyPoint of Contact LeslieEligibility Requirements Citizenship: LPR or U.S. CitizenDegree: Doctoral Degree received within the last 60 months or currently pursuing.Discipline(s):Computer, Information, and Data Sciences (2 )Engineering (2 )Mathematics and Statistics (5 )Other Non-Science & Engineering (1 )Social and Behavioral Sciences (2 )

jobs.title: AI/ Machine Learning Engineering Intern at Gecko Robotics, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Gecko Robotics, Inc. Expires: 10/17/2026 Gecko Robotics is seeking an AI/ML Engineering Intern to join our Engineering team in New York for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.Gecko collects some of the richest inspection data in the world: ultrasonic and other non-destructive testing (NDT) measurements from wall-climbing robots, paired with the documents, drawings, and operational records that describe the assets they inspect. You will work on a defined project that turns that data into decisions, building models and the systems around them that run reliably on real customer data. This is an engineering internship, not an analytics one. We build the systems that analyze the data, not just the analysis.Due to government program requirements, candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.What you will doOwn a scoped machine learning project from problem framing through evaluation and integration, under the guidance of experienced engineers.Build data pipelines in Python that clean, label, and structure NDT sensor data, documents, or operational records for model training and inference.Train, evaluate, and iterate on models, and design evaluations that reflect how the output will be used in the field.Integrate a model or LLM-based workflow into a service or tool that other engineers and Forward Deployment Engineers can use.Investigate failure modes on messy, real-world data, document what you find, and recommend what to fix next.Use version control, code review, testing, and experiment tracking to produce work others can reproduce and build on.Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship.Technologies We UsePython, PyTorch or similar ML frameworks, NumPy and pandas, SQL, LLM APIs and agent frameworks, Git, Linux, and cloud infrastructure (GCP). Depending on the project, you may also work with signal-processing tools for ultrasonic data, document-processing and information-extraction pipelines, or orchestration tools such as Airflow. The specific tools will depend on the assigned project. About YouYou are an engineer who happens to work in machine learning. You care whether a model works on real data, not just on a benchmark, and you are comfortable owning the code around the model: the pipeline, the evaluation, and the integration. You approach new problems methodically, communicate clearly about results and uncertainty, and are excited to be the first person to look at a problem. Required SkillsCurrently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in computer science, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.Ability to work onsite in New York, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.Strong programming experience in Python, including writing well-structured, tested code beyond notebooks.Coursework or project experience in machine learning, including training and evaluating models on real datasets.Working understanding of linear algebra, probability, and statistics.Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain results, quantify uncertainty, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback. Preferred SkillsGraduate-level coursework or research in machine learning, signal processing, or computer vision.Experience taking a model beyond a notebook: building a pipeline, an API, or a tool around it.Experience with LLM APIs, retrieval, information extraction, or document understanding.Experience with time-series or sensor data, especially ultrasonic, acoustic, or other physical measurements.Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP, and to containers such as Docker.Interest in industrial, defense, or infrastructure applications where reliability matters.

jobs.title: Embedded Systems & FPGA Research Intern at OpalAI
jobs.description: Employer: OpalAI Expires: 10/17/2026 OpalAI — NASA SBIR Project: Runtime Health Monitoring for Aerospace SystemsInternship Duration: 3–6 monthsPosition Type: Internship / Research & DevelopmentLocation: Los Angeles, CA / Hybrid, depending on project needsAbout OpalAIOpalAI is a deep-tech company developing Physical AI and intelligent systems for real-world and aerospace environments. Our work spans artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, computer vision, embedded computing, and advanced aerospace technologies.Our team brings experience from organizations including NASA/JPL, Caltech, USC, and UCLA, and we work on federally sponsored R&D programs aimed at translating advanced research into deployable technologies. This internship will support an OpalAI NASA SBIR project focused on improving the reliability and resilience of aerospace computing systems.Beyond traditional aircraft and spacecraft applications, the underlying technologies are also relevant to emerging computing architectures such as space-based data centers, orbital computing infrastructure, autonomous spacecraft, and distributed edge-computing systems, where reliable runtime monitoring, fault detection, and resilient operation are critical.Position OverviewWe are seeking a motivated Embedded Systems & FPGA Research Intern to contribute to a NASA-sponsored Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) project focused on runtime health monitoring and fault detection for safety-critical aerospace systems.The project explores hardware- and software-based techniques for monitoring the runtime behavior, integrity, and operational health of computing systems used in aircraft and spacecraft environments. The intern will work across technologies including embedded firmware, operating systems, runtime analysis, FPGA/RTL design, and system-level monitoring.These capabilities can support a broad range of next-generation aerospace computing platforms, including autonomous spacecraft, high-performance onboard computing, satellite constellations, and future space-based data centers, where systems may need to detect faults and maintain reliable operation with limited human intervention.This position is particularly well suited for a student or recent graduate interested in the intersection of embedded systems, computer architecture, FPGA design, cybersecurity and resilience, autonomous computing, and aerospace systems.ResponsibilitiesDepending on background and project needs, the intern may contribute to several of the following areas:Develop and evaluate techniques for runtime monitoring and analysis of embedded systems and firmware.Analyze firmware and operating-system behavior, You will assist users, business stakeholders, technical teams, and third-party providers to support upgrades and testing, troubleshooting and training, documentation, reporting and data extraction, audit activities, and ongoing system and process improvements.This opportunity will begin Summer 2027, working a full-time schedule (40 hours/week). These opportunities can enhance your academic training while teaching critical business skills and allowing you to learn about BPMI, the Navy, and the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program.Essential Duties:Assist with basic maintenance and administration of BPMI business systems, including enabling and disabling users, managing role permissions, and scheduling reports under close supervision.Support system upgrades by executing test cases, documenting results, and assisting with rollout activities under significant oversight.Assist with system configuration activities by documenting configuration changes and tracking work performed by third-party consultants under supervision.Help coordinate user support activities, including answering basic system usage questions, assisting with troubleshooting, and updating system process documentation.Gather documentation and system information to support internal and external audit requests under significant oversight.Support updating procedures, user guides, training materials, and other documentation to reflect approved system or process changes.Participate in department initiatives related to process improvement, operational effectiveness, and system changes in a supporting role.The essential duties identified are representative but are not intended to be an exhaustive or inclusive list of all the responsibilities of the position.What You Can Expect:A culture that values people through recognition of accomplishments, work-life balance, and a sense of community.A diverse group of talented individuals working toward the common goal of supporting the United States Navy in their pursuit of national security.Competitive and attractive pay and benefits with a stable organization.Opportunities to participate in BPMI sponsored committees and clubs, each with their own mission and purpose.Career advancement and professional development programs.Minimum Job Requirements:Enrolled in Management Information Systems, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Computer Information Systems, Business Intelligence, Information Systems / Technology or related undergraduate degree program from an accredited college or university.Minimum of six (6) semesters completed prior to your internship (~90 credits).Requires a security clearance; however, all qualified candidates will be considered regardless of their current clearance status. (BPMI) is a prime contractor for the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program (NNPP). jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: Product Engineer Intern at OpenGov
jobs.description: Employer: OpenGov Expires: 10/18/2026 About the RoleOpenGov is looking for Product Engineer Interns who are eager to learn what it means to own a product — from customer discovery through delivery. This internship is built around a new kind of role born from AI's ability to handle execution work that once required multiple specialists. What AI cannot do is decide what matters, talk to customers, make the right call in ambiguous situations, or own whether a product succeeds. That is what Product Engineers learn to do — and this internship is where that journey starts.This role is first and foremost about developing product thinking — not becoming a developer. The best interns will be the ones who grow genuinely curious about customers: who they are, what they actually need, and what outcomes depend on solving their problems. The engineering side — using AI-native tooling to write code, build interfaces — is a skill you will be introduced to and encouraged to develop. It is a career accelerator, not a day-one requirement.If you have a background or strong interest in product management, UX design, engineering, or some combination — and you want real ownership of a problem rather than a slide deck — this internship is for you."Product Engineer" is two words — but the first word is the one that matters most. The second is how you get there. The 10-week internship will run from June 7, 2027 through August 13, 2027. What You'll Work OnA scoped product problem: a defined set of customers, problems, and outcomes — sized for a 10–12 week engagement with real impact.Customer discovery: you will conduct or observe customer conversations and translate what you learn into product decisions.User experience flows: you will define interaction patterns within an existing design system and validate them with users.AI-assisted delivery: using AI-native tooling, you will move from intent to spec to working prototype — supported by your team, but accountable for the output.Metrics: you will define what success looks like for your area and track it throughout the internship. How AI Works in This RoleAI-native tooling handles a significant portion of what product managers and designers have historically spent their time on. As an intern, you will be hands-on with these tools from day one:Spec writing: AI drafts the first spec from your intent statement. You learn to review, sharpen, and own what gets built.UX design: AI generates mockups from the design system based on your flow definitions. You make the product decisions within it.Research synthesis: AI clusters and themes interview notes and support data. You interpret what it means and make the call.Release content: AI generates release notes and enablement materials from shipped features. You review and refine them.Test coverage: AI generates test cases from acceptance criteria. You learn to write criteria precise enough to verify.What AI does not do: understand your customers, make the call on what matters, own the outcome, or build the cross-functional trust that makes things ship. That is the job — and what you will be learning. Key ResponsibilitiesParticipate in customer discovery conversations; synthesize what you hear into defensible product decisions.Define user experience flows and interaction patterns within the existing design system.Write intent documents that AI tooling can execute against; review AI-generated specs for accuracy and completeness.Partner with your engineering and product mentor to resolve ambiguity in real time during the development cycle.Track adoption and usage metrics for your scoped area; use them to drive iteration.Present your product area and findings in a final intern showcase — covering the customer problem, what you built, and what you would do next.Surface gaps, risks, and unanswered questions proactively; don't wait to be asked. Qualifications & What We're Looking ForCurrently pursuing a degree in computer science, information systems, product design, HCI, business, or a closely adjacent field — or equivalent self-directed experience.Genuine curiosity about customers and why products succeed or fail; you find yourself asking "who is this for and does it actually solve their problem?"Strong written communication: you can articulate a product decision clearly enough that an engineer and a designer walk away aligned.Comfort with ambiguity and speed: you make reasonable decisions with incomplete information rather than waiting for certainty.Willingness to grow into code fluency using AI-native tooling — you don't need to arrive as a developer, but you must be willing to get there.Prior exposure to product management, UX design, software development, or customer research is a plus — in any form (coursework, projects, prior internships, side work).Familiarity with design tools (Figma, etc.) or development tooling is welcome but not required. CompensationBoston, MA: $30 per hour

nontechnical stakeholders.* Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel or similar data-analysis tools.* Ability to review structured datasets and identify missing, inconsistent, or unusual information.* Strong written and verbal communication skills.* Ability to work effectively in a remote and collaborative environment.## Preferred QualificationsAcademic, internship, research, or project-based exposure to one or more of the following is preferred:* Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, commercial insurance, or Affordable Care Act programs* Risk adjustment, quality improvement, population health, or value-based care* Medical coding or clinical documentation* Claims adjudication or encounter-submission processes* EHR systems and clinical workflows* HIPAA and healthcare data privacy* SQL, Python, jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern - Tools and Prototypes at Quantum Signal AI
jobs.description: Employer: Quantum Signal AI Expires: 10/21/2026 This is a paid internship. Compensation for this position begins at $29.00 per hour.Role Summary: Quantum Signal AI (QSAI) is looking for a Software Engineering Intern – Tools and Prototypes to help develop engineering tooling and prototype software for the summer of 2027. Our applications range from specialized engineering tools to prototypes for advanced vehicle features that are used by engineers, researchers, and designers at Ford and QSAI. Interns will work alongside experienced engineers throughout the software development lifecycle and gain hands-on experience solving real engineering problems in a fast-paced R&D environment. A standout candidate will have experience in compiled languages (C++, Go, etc.), scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, etc.), web development, and software projects outside of an academic setting. We value the ability to quickly learn new technology to meet changing requirements, so a desire to learn is important! Location: Saline, Michigan (In-person). Our “historic schoolhouse” office supports hands-on collaboration, mentorship, and real-time problem solving. What You’ll Do (Essential Functions): Contribute to projects across the full Software Development Lifecycle, from design and implementation, to testing and release management Collaborate within varied project teams to develop tooling to improve engineering workflows Translate ideas, specifications, and/or requirements into high-quality implementations Tackle the challenges of learning, integrating, and leveraging a range of software tools and technologies as needed Develop documentation for software, processes, and projects Create and maintain build processes and CI/CD pipelines What You’ll Bring (Minimum Requirements): Current enrollment in an undergraduate degree-seeking program, pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field Maintaining student status for the entire duration of the internship, including the academic term immediately following the internship Strong understanding of computer science fundamentals including data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, debugging, networking, and file systems Previous work/internship or academic club experience developing software Proficiency developing software in a compiled language (C++, Go, etc.) Experience with scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, etc.) Experience working in both Linux- and Windows-based environments Familiarity with web development (HTML, CSS, JS, etc.) Bonus Points For: Coursework or equivalent experience in operating systems, databases, compilers, concurrency, and other high level computer science topics Experience with REST APIs, either through integrating with existing APIs or designing APIs for downstream consumers Experience with modern web development frameworks and technologies (Node.js, React, Typescript, Flask, etc.) Experience with cloud-based development/deployment via GCP or equivalent cloud provider Experience integrating Identity and Access Management (IAM) solutions into an application (Microsoft Entra, RBAC, MSAL, authentication and authorization APIs) You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you are excited about this role and think you can bring value to Quantum Signal AI, we encourage you to apply! What You’ll Get: Frequent collaboration with a diverse set of teams at QSAI A rare level of work variety and hands-on experience A relaxed, fun community and environment in which to solve interesting problems Opportunity to participate in a 401(k) savings plan Ford AX-Plan vehicle discounts Mentorship-focused learning that emphasizes engineering fundamentals, hands-on problem solving, and understanding the underlying principles behind the systems we build. Other perks to fuel creativity such as an on-site gymnasium, free drinks and snacks, and a variety of optional team activities Candidates for positions with Quantum Signal AI must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. About QSAI: Founded in 1999, Quantum Signal grew up developing intelligent algorithms and AI. As our engineering R&D services expanded, we later sharpened our focus on applications and technology related to mobility, sensing, perception, autonomy, and simulation. In 2019 we became Quantum Signal AI, a subsidiary of Ford Motor developing technologies to advance their R&D efforts. We build solutions to enhance the capability, robustness, safety, and acceptance of intelligent ground vehicles in an effort to make transportation more effective and efficient for all. While AI is part of our name, our internship program emphasizes building fundamental engineering knowledge, analytical thinking, and practical problem-solving skills. We want interns to understand how and why systems work through hands-on experience, mentorship, and experimentation, rather than simply relying on tools to provide answers. Our HQ in the historic Union School in Saline, MI is the perfect playground to develop this cutting-edge technology and we’re always looking for smart folks who like new challenges, learning new skills, and technical variety.

jobs.title: C++ Software Developer Intern at Scalp Trade
jobs.description: Employer: Scalp Trade Expires: 10/21/2026 We are seeking a driven and intellectually curious C++ Software Developer Intern to join our dynamic trading firm. This is an exceptional opportunity to gain hands-on experience building high-performance trading systems while contributing meaningfully to our operations. You will work closely with experienced engineers in a mentorship-rich environment, learning cutting-edge low-latency systems design, trading infrastructure, and modern C++ development practices. This internship is designed to accelerate your growth as a software engineer while you help develop tools and strategies that directly impact our trading operations. If you thrive on learning, enjoy solving complex technical problems, and want to understand how financial technology works at scale, this is the role for you. Key Responsibilities & Learning Objectives Develop and Optimize Components: Under mentor guidance, design and implement features for automated trading systems, with emphasis on understanding the 'why' behind architectural decisions in high-performance environments.Collaborative Development: Contribute to core trading platform enhancements alongside senior engineers, learning best practices for low-latency, distributed systems.Code Quality & Design: Learn and apply SOLID principles, modern C++ patterns, and system design concepts through hands-on code reviews and pair programming sessions.Performance Analysis: Participate in profiling and optimizing trading system components; understand tuning techniques for real-time operations.Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Document code, design decisions, and lessons learned to build your technical communication skills.Problem-Solving: Work on well-scoped technical challenges that build your analytical and debugging skills in a production environment. Required Skills & QualificationsStrong Foundation in C++: Solid grasp of C++ fundamentals (STL, memory management, move semantics, templates). Production experience not required; demonstrated projects or coursework show readiness.Core CS Fundamentals: Comfortable with data structures, algorithms, and basic systems concepts (threading, process synchronization).Quick Learner: Able to rapidly pick up new tools, libraries, and frameworks with minimal guidance.Linux Familiarity: Comfortable working in Linux environments; shell scripting and command-line tools are a plus.Collaborative Mindset: Excellent communication skills; eager to learn from mentors and ask clarifying questions. Preferred Skills Multi-threading Experience: Practical familiarity with concurrent programming, thread safety, and synchronization primitives.Network Programming: Exposure to socket programming, TCP/IP, or distributed system basics.Additional Languages: Proficiency in Python, C#, or other systems languages broadens your perspective.Financial Markets Interest: Curiosity about trading, equities, options, or how financial markets work—we teach the rest.Database Exposure: Familiarity with SQL or understanding of how databases store and retrieve data at scale.Version Control & Tooling: Experience with Git, debugging tools (gdb, valgrind), or profilers (perf, flamegraph). Personal Attributes Intellectual Curiosity: Genuine interest in understanding how systems work, from code to infrastructure to business outcomes.Growth Mindset: Embrace challenges and feedback as opportunities to learn. We expect you to grow significantly over the internship.Ownership & Initiative: Proactive in seeking learning opportunities and taking on well-scoped responsibilities with minimal oversight.Adaptability: Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid changes; thriving in a fast-paced, high-performance environment.Collaborative Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills with a preference for brainstorming and learning from teammates.Passion for Technology: Excitement about staying current with modern C++ and high-performance systems. What You'll GainHands-On Production Experience: Work in a real, production trading environment—not a sandbox. Your code runs strategies that generate revenue.Mentorship from Experts: Learn directly from senior engineers with deep expertise in low-latency systems, C++, and financial technology.Comprehensive Technical Knowledge: Understand high-performance systems design, from kernel tuning to network stack optimization.Career Acceleration: Build a portfolio of impactful projects and establish relationships with leaders in fintech.Potential for Conversion: Strong performers are considered for full-time roles upon graduation or at the conclusion of the internship. Compensation: This internship is paid at $7,000 per month for the program.

jobs.title: Engineering Intern- Summer 2027 at Medtronic
jobs.description: Employer: Medtronic Expires: 10/21/2026 CAREERS THAT CHANGE LIVES Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact. Our summer internships are full-time (40 hours/week), paid positions lasting 10-11 weeks. We offer competitive compensation, educational and social programming throughout the summer, as well as housing assistance and relocation support for eligible interns. Engineering Intern Opportunities for Students Interns may support one or more engineering areas based on business need, candidate background, and location availability. Examples of work in each area are listed below. Research & Development Engineering Support design, development, analysis, and testing of engineering solutions during research and product development phases. Contribute to system integration, verification, validation, risk analysis, and data-driven evaluation efforts. Support safety testing, regulatory compliance, and transfer of products from development into manufacturing. Great for students who want to: Gain exposure to how new medical technologies move from early concepts through validation and manufacturing readiness. Apply engineering fundamentals to real design, testing, and system-level challenges. Understand how safety, quality, and regulatory requirements influence engineering decisions. Operations Engineering Design and support manufacturing processes, procedures, and production layouts for assemblies, equipment, machining, and material handling. Provide technical and sustaining engineering support within manufacturing environments, including equipment and process improvements. Contribute to continuous improvement efforts focused on quality, efficiency, and production yield. Great for students who want to: Learn how products are built, assembled, and scaled for full-scale manufacturing. See how engineering decisions directly impact production efficiency, cost, and output. Gain hands-on experience solving process and equipment challenges in a manufacturing setting. Quality Engineering Develop, apply, and maintain quality standards and protocols for materials, components, and finished products. Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to support quality requirements and compliance. Support reliability studies, data analysis, and evaluation of design or test methods to achieve product reliability targets. Great for students who want to: Understand how quality systems and standards help ensure medical products are safe and compliant. Work cross-functionally to support quality and reliability across the product lifecycle. Build experience using data, testing, and process evaluation to support engineering decisions. Location and Work Model Most internship positions are based at primary hubs in Minnesota, California, Colorado, Connecticut, and Massachusetts, with additional opportunities available in Arizona, Florida, Michigan, Tennessee, and Texas. Candidate location preferences are strongly considered during the interview and offer process; however, flexibility increases the number of potential opportunities available. All interns must reside in the U.S. for the duration of the internship. Interns are expected to work onsite a minimum of 4 days per week and participate full time, 40 hours per week, as part of the intern cohort from June 1 through August 13 for semester system programs or June 14 through August 20 for quarter system programs. Required Qualifications Working toward a bachelor's or master's degree in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related engineering discipline with an anticipated graduation date of Winter 2027, Spring 2028, Winter 2028, or Spring 2029. Applicants for Medtronic’s Summer Internship Program must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Medtronic does not sponsor work authorization for internship positions. Individuals on temporary visa classifications, including E, F‑1 (CPT or OPT), H‑1, H‑2, L, B, J, or TN, as well as anyone who requires employment sponsorship now or in the future, are not eligible for the Program. Preferred Qualifications Prior experience in engineering design, testing, manufacturing, quality, data analysis, or product development through internships, academic projects, research, laboratory work, or relevant work experience. Experience with engineering software, programming, CAD, data analysis, or laboratory equipment. Experience creating technical documentation, laboratory reports, project summaries, test reports, or engineering presentations. Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale. Flexibility in geographic location. Physical Job Requirements: The physical demands described within the Responsibilities section of this job description are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of the role, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer and communicate with peers and coworkers.
